name: sightread
description: A reading lens for code: highlight, dim, fold and outline function segments to help you understand code in place.

viewsWelcome.contents:
$(bookmark) Mark the selection — ⌘K 1 yellow · ⌘K 2 red · ⌘K C any color · ⌘K N color + note.
$(sparkle) The button above runs Interpret Current (AI): role-colored signposts across the function, class or file you're reading.

$(bookmark) Mark the selection — Ctrl+K 1 yellow · Ctrl+K 2 red · Ctrl+K C any color · Ctrl+K N color + note.
$(sparkle) The button above runs Interpret Current (AI): role-colored signposts across the function, class or file you're reading.

Definition and reference jumps you make while this view is open build the call tree you walked.
$(map) The button above finds logic routes (AI): type a goal, get a planned path that lights up as you read.

walkthroughs.title: Read code with SightRead
walkthroughs.description: Spotlight, mark, and let AI mark what's worth reading.

steps.title: Turn on the spotlight
steps.description:
Dim everything except what you're reading. The recommended level keeps the cursor's block plus related blocks lit — the eye in the status bar shows the current level and switches it on click.
[Choose Spotlight Level](command:sightread.spotlightSelect)

media.altText: Editor with most lines dimmed while the current segment stays lit

steps.title: Mark what matters
steps.description:
Select lines and mark them in one of five colors — the editor's right-click menu has the color and note variants, and each color has its own command for a custom keybinding.
[Mark Selection](command:sightread.markPickColor)

media.altText: Code lines carrying yellow, red and green markers, the yellow one with a note

steps.title: See the function's structure
steps.description:
The Segments view mirrors the function under your cursor — branches, loops, guards — and follows you as you move. Collapsing a segment folds the code with it.
[Open Segments View](command:sightread.segmentsView.focus)

media.altText: Segments tree beside the editor, the selected segment highlighted in both

steps.title: Let AI mark what's worth reading
steps.description:
Steps arrive role-colored with a signpost note on each — why the code exists, not what it says. Needs a coding-agent CLI (claude, codex, …) on your PATH; SightRead probes for one automatically.
[Interpret Current](command:sightread.interpretFunction)

media.altText: Numbered role-colored step badges beside code blocks, each with a short note

steps.title: Your reading leaves a trail
steps.description:
While the Trail view is open, jumps to definitions and references build the call tree you actually walked. Click a node to jump back to it.
[Open Trail View](command:sightread.trailView.focus)

media.altText: A small call tree with the current node selected and the visited path emphasized

steps.title: Start from the entrances
steps.description:
Entry points are what the outside world calls in this file. A CodeLens above each one counts its external references — click it to peek them, or list every entry at once.
[Go to Entry Point](command:sightread.goToEntry)

media.altText: Entry declarations annotated with reference counts, one dimmed as suspected

sightread.guide.harness.markdownDescription:
Which coding-agent CLI interprets functions. Accepted values:
- `auto` *(default)* — probes the PATH and takes the first hit, in market-share order: `claude` → `codex` → `opencode` → `pi` → `cursor` → `devin` → `aider` → `agy` (running inside Cursor promotes `cursor` to the front)
- a builtin harness name: `claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `pi`, `cursor`, `devin`, `aider`, `agy`
- the name of an entry in `#sightread.guide.customHarnesses#`

sightread.guide.model.markdownDescription: Model for AI runs, appended to every harness invocation as `--model <value>` — the one flag all builtin harnesses share. The value's vocabulary belongs to the chosen harness: `claude` takes `sonnet` / `opus` / a full model id, `opencode` and `pi` take `provider/model`, `agy` takes a model slug and fails loudly on unknown ones. Empty *(default)* = each CLI's own default model (the progress notification then shows `default model`).

sightread.guide.language.markdownDescription: Language of the notes and summary in AI-generated guides (e.g. `简体中文`, `Japanese`, `Deutsch`). Empty *(default)* = English.

sightread.guide.promptTemplate.function.markdownDescription:
Custom reading instructions when interpreting a **function**.

Empty *(default)* = builtin rules: structure roles (main / setup / fallback / special), plus the existence-reason of at most 9 core entities.

Placeholders:
- `${filePath}` — file path relative to the workspace
- `${languageId}` — programming language
- `${subjectName}` — the function's name
- `${subjectText}` — its source with absolute line numbers
- `${fileHeader}` — the file's import region
- `${userNote}` — what you type into the per-run focus box

The JSON output contract is appended by SightRead after the template and always wins on conflict.

sightread.guide.promptTemplate.class.markdownDescription:
Custom reading instructions when interpreting a **class**.

Empty *(default)* = builtin rules: one step per member, role-tagged (entry / helper / util / lifecycle / state), notes give the member's reason to exist.

Same placeholders as `#sightread.guide.promptTemplate.function#` — `${subjectName}` / `${subjectText}` are the class's name and source.

The JSON output contract is appended by SightRead and always wins on conflict.

sightread.guide.promptTemplate.file.markdownDescription:
Custom reading instructions when interpreting a whole **file**.

Empty *(default)* = builtin rules: one step per top-level block, role-tagged (config / types / core / wiring / util / exports), notes give the block's reason to exist.

Same placeholders as `#sightread.guide.promptTemplate.function#` — `${subjectName}` / `${subjectText}` are the file's basename and source.

The JSON output contract is appended by SightRead and always wins on conflict.

sightread.guide.promptTemplate.route.markdownDescription:
Custom exploration instructions when **finding logic routes** from a typed goal.

Empty *(default)* = builtin rules: start at an entry, follow the call/dependency chain, attach only critical side references, at most 12 hops.

Placeholder: `${goal}` — the goal typed into the input box. The symbol under the cursor is appended after the template, so the goal may just say "it".

The JSON output contract is appended by SightRead after the template and always wins on conflict.

sightread.guide.promptTemplate.trace.markdownDescription:
Custom exploration instructions when **tracing entries** to the code under the cursor.

Empty *(default)* = builtin rules: find at most 3 relevant entry points and route each chain down to the queried code.

Placeholders: `${filePath}`, `${subjectName}`, `${startLine}`, `${endLine}` — the queried code's location.

The JSON output contract is appended by SightRead after the template and always wins on conflict.

sightread.guide.customHarnesses.markdownDescription:
Extra harness profiles, or wholesale replacements of builtin ones (same name wins). Each value is an object with:
- `command` — the executable
- `args` — argument array; `${prompt}` is replaced with the full prompt (omit it to pipe the prompt via stdin)
- `exploreArgs` — argument array for read-only repository exploration; declaring it enables route planning *(optional)*
- `env` — extra environment variables *(optional)*
- `resultField` — field of a JSON-envelope stdout holding the final text *(optional; omit for CLIs that print the plain answer)*
- `errorField` — envelope field that is `true` on failure *(optional)*

Example:
```json
{ "mytool": { "command": "mytool", "args": ["run", "${prompt}"] } }
```

enumDescriptions: Segment + Variables — the cursor's block plus blocks touched by the symbol under the cursor stay lit (recommended)
Segment — only the cursor's block stays lit
Function — everything outside the current function is dimmed
sightread.spotlight.defaultMode.markdownDescription: Spotlight level applied on startup. Switch anytime via the status-bar eye, the Segments view button, or `SightRead: Spotlight: Choose Level…`.

sightread.spotlight.functionDimOpacity.markdownDescription: Opacity of code **outside the current function** while the spotlight is on. `0` hides it entirely, `1` disables this dim tier.

sightread.spotlight.segmentDimOpacity.markdownDescription: Opacity of **unrelated parts inside the current function** (levels Segment and up).

sightread.spotlight.siblingDimOpacity.markdownDescription: Opacity of the **sibling blocks** of the cursor's block (levels Segment and up) — slightly brighter than the unrelated parts, keeping nearby structure readable.

enumDescriptions: Vivid — brighter, higher-chroma accents; marks stand out at a glance
Soft — same hues with the chroma reined in; annotations recede, code stays the protagonist
sightread.palette.markdownDescription: Color band for every mark accent — the 5 manual colors and the AI role colors, each with dark/light theme variants. Editor decorations and view swatches follow the setting live. Sidebar **label tints** come from contributed theme colors (`sightread.marker*` / `sightread.guide*`) whose defaults stay on the vivid values — override them via `#workbench.colorCustomizations#` if you want soft labels too.

enumDescriptions: Before the code — shifts that line's code to the right
At the end of the line, after the code
sightread.marker.notePosition.markdownDescription: Where a mark's note renders on its first marked line.

sightread.entries.codeLens.markdownDescription: Show a CodeLens above each entry-point declaration (`» entry — 3 external refs`); clicking it peeks the references. Entries are the symbols the outside world calls in this file — `SightRead: Go to Entry Point…` lists them on demand.

sightread.entries.showSuspected.markdownDescription: Also show **suspected** entries — symbols with no references found anywhere. These may be framework-invoked entries (activation hooks, route handlers) or dead code.

sightread.entries.languageHints.markdownDescription: Use language syntax (`export`/`pub` keywords, Go capitalization, leading-underscore naming) to classify symbols that have no references anywhere: declared-public ones become entries, declared-private ones are dropped.

sightread.variableTint.enabled.markdownDescription: Outline all occurrences of the symbol under the cursor within the enclosing function — reads in blue, writes in orange.
